title: Cache Persistence
description: Persist React Query cache across page reloads and browser sessions for offline-capable applications.

data.text: By default, React Query cache lives entirely in memory. When the user refreshes the page, closes the tab, or restarts the browser, all cached data is lost. Persistence plugins save the cache to a durable storage medium, allowing the app to show cached data immediately on reload â€” even while offline. This dramatically improves perceived performance and enables true offline-first experiences.

data.title: Instant Loads with Persistence
data.text: With cache persistence, your app can render content before the network even responds. Users see cached data instantly while React Query validates freshness in the background. This is the same technique used by native mobile apps and progressive web apps.

React Query supports multiple storage backends through its persister plugins. The two most common are localStorage (simple, synchronous, limited capacity) and IndexedDB (asynchronous, large capacity). Choose based on your dataset size and performance needs.

terms.definition: An object that handles serializing and deserializing the React Query cache to and from a storage medium.
The process of restoring the query cache from persisted storage when the app initializes.
A wrapper component that manages cache persistence and hydration automatically.

data.text: The `createSyncStoragePersister` utility from `@tanstack/query-sync-storage-persister` wraps localStorage for simple persistence. It is synchronous, so hydration happens immediately on app load. Use this for small to medium datasets.

data.title: localStorage persistence setup
data.content: Wrap your app with PersistQueryClientProvider for automatic cache persistence.

data.text: On app initialization, the persister reads stored data and hydrates the query cache. Components can render immediately with cached data while React Query validates freshness in the background. If the storage is empty or corrupted, the cache starts fresh.

data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App
    participant Persister
    participant Storage
    participant QueryClient
    App->>Persister: Initialize
    Persister->>Storage: Read cached data
    Storage-->>Persister: Return stored cache
    Persister->>QueryClient: Hydrate cache
    QueryClient-->>App: Cache ready
    App->>App: Render with cached data
    App->>QueryClient: Background refetch stale queries
    QueryClient-->>App: Updated data
data.caption: Cache hydration sequence on app initialization.

data.title: Security Warning
data.text: Never persist sensitive data like auth tokens, personal information, or payment details in localStorage or IndexedDB. These storage mechanisms are accessible to any script on the page and persist across sessions. Use secure, HTTP-only cookies for sensitive data.

data.title: Exercise: Add Persistence to an Existing App
data.description: Add cache persistence to a React Query app that currently has no persistence. Measure the perceived load time before and after.
steps: Create a QueryClient with a 1-hour cacheTime.
Create a persister using localStorage with a unique cache key.
Wrap your app root with PersistQueryClientProvider.
Verify cached data appears instantly on page reload.
data.expectedOutcome: Data appears instantly on reload instead of showing a loading spinner, confirming successful persistence.

items.question: Does persistence work with server-side rendering (SSR)?
items.answer: Persistence plugins are client-side only. In SSR apps, wrap PersistQueryClientProvider inside a dynamic import with ssr: false to avoid server-side execution.

items.question: Can I use multiple persisters at once?
items.answer: Yes, you can chain persisters or write a custom persister that delegates to multiple storage backends. React Query supports any storage interface that implements getItem, setItem, and removeItem.

items.question: How do I clear the persisted cache?
items.answer: Call persister.removeClient() or clear the storage key directly: localStorage.removeItem('react-query-cache-v1'). You can also call queryClient.clear() to wipe the in-memory cache.

data.title: Cache Persistence Key Points
points: Persistence survives page reloads, tab closes, and browser restarts.
localStorage is simple and synchronous but limited to ~5 MB.
Hydration restores the cache on app initialization.
Never persist sensitive data in plain storage.
data.takeaway: Cache persistence dramatically improves perceived performance and enables offline-first experiences.
